To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the damped oscillator cepstral features (DOCC and SyDOCC) outperform the baseline cepstral features in noise and channel-degraded speech-recognition tasks.
the DOCC and SyDOCC features improve speech recognition performance over the baseline features in all conditions and that the SyDOCC feature performs better than DOCC in all conditions.
the proposed DOCC and SyDOCC features improve the performance of the baseline melcepstrum in all noise and channel conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of robust speech features that are based on auditory models of speech production and perception.
the design of new features that are robust to noise and channel distortion.
the development of new features for robust speech-recognition tasks that have a biological motivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed features outperform the baseline and the other published noise robust cepstral features in the Aurora4 noise and channel degraded speech recognition task.
the DOCC feature is more robust in noise, the SyDOCC feature is more channel robust, and the DOCC feature performs better in the presence of both noise and channel distortion.
the proposed features have shown to improve the robustness of the speech recognizer in all conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed features outperformed other features in terms of recognition accuracy and robustness.
we are able to achieve a 20% reduction in the word error rate for the noisy condition and a 10% reduction in the channel-degraded condition.
our proposed DOCC and SyDOCC features have the potential to improve the robustness of automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems in noisy conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DOCC and SyDOCC features can be used as an alternative to the conventional melcepstral feature.
the DOCC and SyDOCC feature sets can be used in conjunction with any other robust feature set to improve the performance of the baseline robust feature set.
we have shown that a new set of features can be derived using a physiological inspired signal-processing technique and the features are robust to noise.
